items.title: Russell holds off Verstappen by 0.196s to win in Baku
items.summary: George Russell converted pole into victory in the 51-lap Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with Max Verstappen second and Isack Hadjar third on his return to Red Bull. Kimi Antonelli recovered from 16th on the grid (after a Q1 crash) to finish fifth. The official standings now list Antonelli on 302 points and Russell on 236, a 66-point gap, down from 81 before the race.
items.why_it_matters: Russell's win narrows the championship gap and Hadjar's podium is his first since returning from the sidelines; the standings figures are current post-race totals, not a pre-weekend snapshot.

items.title: Norris wants a race ban for Colapinto after the Turn 1 pile-up that ended his race
items.summary: Franco Colapinto locked up entering Turn 1 on the second Safety Car restart, hit team-mate Pierre Gasly, and the chain reaction also collected Lando Norris's McLaren; all three retired. The FIA's Document 66 confirms a 10-second time penalty, converted to a five-place grid drop at Colapinto's next race (Bahrain). Norris said afterwards the FIA should hand out race bans for this kind of driving, though the current points-based ban threshold (12 points in 12 months) means no such sanction applies under today's rules.
items.why_it_matters: It ended the race for a reigning champion and two Alpine cars, the ruling is now confirmed rather than press-reported, and Norris's public call for tougher sanctions is a live sporting-conduct storyline distinct from the published penalty.

items.title: Antonelli calls Baku his 'worst weekend of the season' as title lead shrinks
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli crashed in Q1 and started 16th, then carried floor damage from Safety Car restart contact with Oliver Bearman before recovering to fifth. He said the weekend was damage limitation rather than a strong drive, as team-mate Russell's win cut his championship lead from 81 to 66 points with several rounds remaining.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first time all season the young points leader has openly described a weekend as his worst, and the shrinking gap keeps Russell mathematically live in the title fight.

items.title: Vasseur pushes back on Ferrari leadership speculation fuelled by Horner comments
items.summary: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur said the team is not working 'in perfect serenity' amid ongoing questions about his future, referencing former Red Bull boss Christian Horner's recent remark that Ferrari is the one team he would want to run. Vasseur reaffirmed his commitment to Ferrari, which finished P4 (Leclerc) and P6 (Hamilton) in Baku, while saying the constant speculation is a distraction for the garage.
items.why_it_matters: It is an ongoing leadership-uncertainty storyline at one of the grid's top teams, running in parallel with Ferrari's on-track power-unit deficit this season.

items.title: Alpine release statement over online hate and abuse following Azerbaijan GP
items.summary: Alpine issued a statement condemning "hate and abuse" directed at Franco Colapinto online after his Turn 1 restart collision took out team-mate Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris's McLaren. The team has not disclosed further internal action against Colapinto beyond the confirmed FIA sanction (Document 66: 10-second penalty converted to a five-place grid drop at Bahrain).
items.why_it_matters: It is a separate team-level response to online abuse, distinct from the FIA's own ruling and from Norris's public call for tougher sporting sanctions; do not conflate the two or imply Alpine has announced any additional driver discipline.
